$comment: Rebuilt 2026-08-16. The evidence behind every structural choice is in
HealthOS/knowledge/training-programme-evidence.md. If a decision here is not defensible from a
row in that file, it should not be here.
The four changes that matter:
1. EVERY MAIN PATTERN NOW APPEARS TWICE A WEEK, heavy on one day and light/technical on the
other. Pelland 2025 (67 studies, 2,058 participants): with volume equated, frequency has
negligible effect on SIZE but a 100% posterior probability of raising STRENGTH. Strength is
the stated non-negotiable ('I don't want to lose track of my main lifts'), so the main lifts
get the frequency and the arms and calves do not. Total sets per day are unchanged.
2. BB ROW AND OVERHEAD PRESS MOVED TO FRESH SLOTS. BB row sat 165 lb x 8 on 2026-05-25 and
165 lb x 8 on 2026-08-15: twelve weeks, zero movement, always the fourth or fifth block.
Overhead press went 60x10 to 65x7, which is net flat. Both now lead or sit second.
3. THE HANDSTAND LADDER IS GONE. Never logged once in 427 sets.
4. EVERY PAIRING IS NOW PHYSICALLY POSSIBLE, and a validator proves it rather than an author
remembering. See `station` on every exercise and equipment.json for the rule.
Frontal-plane work is loaded (lateral lunge, lateral bound, Copenhagen), not banded burnout.
Comert & Gruber 2025 found hip strengthening ALONE had minimal effect on knee alignment, which
is exactly what the banded lateral walk was. It is now insurance for the running, not a hobby.
Conditioning (run, bike, swim) is NOT in this file. It lives in conditioning.json because it is
not organised by gym day and does not share the set/rep/rest shape.
REBUILT 2026-08-21, after a per-session read of the watch export. Sessions run 81 to 120 minutes
with 45 to 75% of every one below 110 bpm, and Thursday 20 August contains a 28-minute hole
between squat set 3 and the next logged set. The sessions are long because of REST, not work:
roughly 4 to 5 minutes of actual lifting inside 81 minutes.
THE SUPERSETS WERE NOT SUPERSETS, and he said so himself. Eleven of the thirteen "alternate"
blocks were one real lift plus a band, a plank, a bridge or a carry, while the app told him
"Superset: alternate the two, rest once after both". They are now `pairing: "fill"`, which says
the true thing: do the partner IN the lift rest gaps, it adds no time. That is not a demotion,
it is the mechanism that shortens the session, and it is why these partners no longer consume a
time budget.
THE TWO "REAL PAIRS" THE ANALYSIS ASKED FOR ARE PHYSICALLY IMPOSSIBLE and were not built. It
called for chest press with row, and overhead press with pulldown. In this gym the row holds a
rack and the chest press holds a machine; the overhead press is at the dumbbells and the pulldown
at the cable stack. validate.mjs already refuses an alternate block that spans two zones or
occupies two fixtures, a gate written after the programme made that mistake five times. The
analysis was produced without the equipment model. Every existing pair is a lift plus a
fixture-free partner because that is the ONLY pair this gym physically permits, so the shape was
a constraint being obeyed rather than a defect. Two blocks are genuine loaded alternates and were
left alone: Monday split-squat with suitcase carry, and Monday lateral lunge with calf raise.
THE TYPED `time` FIELD IS GONE. It said "75-85 min" on days the app own budget model puts at 100
to 106, and the watch says his real sessions run 81 to 120. The typed string was the only one of
the three that nothing could check. It is computed and decomposed on the page now.
EVERY BLOCK CARRIES `why`, one line, required by the validator. He said the programme reads as
arbitrary because he had never seen the evidence file, and a programme he does not believe is one
he stops finishing. Where a block has no evidence behind it the line is SUPPOSED to say so.
Audited 2026-08-27: it does not. The honest admissions are the Monday calf raise and the
Copenhagen. The carries, the single-leg work, the four-times-a-week glute bridge, the shoulder
taps and the five dumbbell partners invented on 2026-08-22 are equally unsourced and admit
nothing. This list also used to name "rotator cuff", which has not been a block in this file
since the bands moved to warmups.json.
EVERY BLOCK IS A PAIR, from 2026-08-22, and 22 of the 25 are supersets. Friday "Biceps, then
Carry" is deliberately `sequence` and its own `why` explains why. An earlier version of this
heading read "EVERY BLOCK IS A SUPERSET", three lines above the exception. Sourced:
Iversen VM, Norum M, Schoenfeld BJ, Fimland MS. No Time to Lift? Designing Time-Efficient
Training Programs for Strength and Hypertrophy: A Narrative Review. Sports Medicine 2021.
- "superset training can be performed in approximately half the time as traditional training
without compromising training volume".
- Robbins et al., 15 trained males, 8 weeks, bench press and bench pull at 3 to 6 reps,
superset vs traditional. Bench press +2.4 +/- 1.8% superset vs +2.3 +/- 1.9% traditional;
bench pull +2.2 +/- 1.1% vs +1.2 +/- 1.7%. Same strength, roughly half the time.
- The review is honest that these techniques are "probably better at inducing hypertrophy than
muscular strength, and more research is needed on longitudinal training effects". The one
loaded 8-week trial above is the reason this is safe for a strength goal, not a claim that
supersets BUILD more strength.
- "antagonist preloading potentially can facilitate increased neural activation, which acutely
increases strength performance". That is why the partner is always a muscle the lead lift is
NOT using, rather than whatever fills a gap in the spreadsheet.
Three rules decide every partner in this file, and between them there is nothing left to guess:
1. THE PARTNER IS A MUSCLE THE LEAD LIFT DOES NOT USE. Triceps in a pull, biceps in a press,
side delts in anything, calves in an upper-body lift, upper body in a jump. Per the review
this protects the lead lift and may help it.
2. THE PARTNER IS CARRIED, NEVER FIXED. Dumbbells and kettlebells go with him to any station,
which is his own constraint: "everywhere that I go I can take a dumbbell or pair of
dumbbells or kettlebell with me. It is just that I am not going to go ahead on the cable
section and bring a mat." So almost every partner is `station: null`, and the cable section
and machine bank are no longer dead ends. NINE PARTNER PLACEMENTS DO NEED THE FLOOR, though:
the glute bridge four times, the dead bug three, the shoulder taps and the Copenhagen once
each. All nine sit in zones equipment.json marks `floor: true`, so nothing is illegal and the
validator is right to pass them. His constraint was about the CABLE section specifically, and
an earlier version of this line generalised it into "needs no floor" and then broke the
general version nine times while honouring the specific one. The Copenhagen also occupies a
bench, which makes it the one partner holding a fixture.
3. THE PARTNER IS LOGGED AND THE NUMBER MOVES. Five of the ELEVEN distinct partners are
dumbbell exercises progressed by weight. The other six are not, and three of those print a
rep count that never moves: the glute bridge at 2x12/leg, the dead bug at 3x10/side, the
shoulder taps at 3x30. An earlier version of this line said "all five", which counted only
the cases that complied. Nothing goes in a session that cannot be progressively overloaded;
that is what put the bands in warmups.json on 2026-08-21 and it is not being undone, though
four band exercises remain as swap ALTERNATIVES here and were never reconciled against it.

monday.name: Monday
monday.title: Lower A: squat heavy, second hinge
monday.desc: Squat heavy, hinge light, sideways loaded

blocks.label: Power Primer

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.cue: Stand a forearm's length from the box. Swing the arms back, bend the knees about a quarter of the way, and jump ONTO the box. Land with both feet flat and knees bent, quietly. Then STEP down one foot at a time, never jump down. Success looks like: you hear almost nothing when you land, and you could hold the landing still for two seconds. If you land with a thud or stumble, the box is too high. Three reps only, because this is about speed, not tiredness.

alts.name: Lateral Bound
alts.cue: Hop sideways off one foot, land on the other, and freeze completely still for two seconds before hopping back. Only go as far as you can land and freeze. 3x4 each side.

alts.name: Pogo Hops
alts.cue: Small fast bounces off the balls of your feet. Keep the ankles stiff and the knees almost straight, like a skipping rope without the rope. 3x15.

alts.name: Explosive Step-Up
alts.cue: One foot on the box. Drive up fast enough that the other foot leaves the ground at the top, then lower slowly. No jumping, so no landing. Use this if anything hurts. 3x5 each leg.

open.q: The card says 3 sets of 3 and on 2026-08-27 you logged 10 reps a set. One of the two is wrong and nobody has established which. Note #20 asks how to progress these: a taller box is not the answer (stepping down removes the landing, so height mostly buys a deeper tuck, not more force) and neither is more reps. What is left is intent and ground contact time, and NO trial was found for that ladder, so it is not going on a card until it is sourced. How many did you mean to do?

blocks.why: Jumps first, while fresh. Deng 2024, 21 studies in untrained people: 0.61 for strength and 0.61 for aerobic fitness at 2 to 3 sessions a week. Box jump, because you step down out of it instead of absorbing a landing at your bodyweight.

blocks.label: Main Lift: Back Squat

exercises.name: BB Back Squat
exercises.cue: The lift we are progressing. Stance slightly wider than your hips with the toes turned out a little. Breathe IN and hold it, tighten your stomach like you are about to be poked, then sit down between your feet until the crease of your hip is below the top of your knee. Knees push out over your second toe, they do not fall inward. Stand up and breathe out at the top. Take a fresh breath and re-tighten before EVERY rep, not just the first.

alts.name: Smith Squat
alts.cue: The bar runs on rails so it cannot drift. Set your feet slightly in front of the bar. Same breathing, same depth.

alts.name: Front Squat
alts.cue: Bar rests on the front of your shoulders, elbows pointed forward and high. Because the weight is in front, your body stays more upright and depth comes easier. Much lighter than a back squat.

alts.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
alts.cue: Hold the heaviest dumbbell you can at your chest like a cup. The front weight balances you so you sit deeper. Use this if the racks are all taken.

alts.name: Leg Press
alts.cue: Feet shoulder width on the platform. Lower until your knees are near your chest without your lower back rounding off the pad, then press. Use this on a day your back is tired.

blocks.why: Squat is one of the four patterns that earns twice a week. Pelland 2025, 67 studies: strength rises with frequency at matched volume (posterior 100%), size does not care about the split.

blocks.label: Second Pattern: Hinge

exercises.name: DB Romanian Deadlift
exercises.cue: This is the SECOND time this week you hinge, and it is deliberately light: roughly what you did for 6 on Thursday minus 30 to 40 lb. The job is a clean groove, not a hard set. Bar touching your legs the whole way, knees slightly bent and then FROZEN. Push your hips backward toward the wall behind you until you feel a strong stretch down the back of your thighs, usually around knee height. Then squeeze your bum and drive the hips forward to stand. Stop the moment your lower back wants to round. No straps needed on this one: it is light on purpose, and if the bar is slipping at this weight the weight is wrong, not your hands.

alts.name: Back Extension
alts.cue: On the 45 degree pad. Hinge down and squeeze your bum to come up. Hug a plate for load.

alts.name: Kettlebell Swing
alts.cue: Same hip snap, done fast. Hike the bell back between your legs, then SNAP the hips forward so the bell floats to chest height. Arms do nothing. Start at 35 lb. 2x12.

open.q: This was a second BB Romanian Deadlift called light, at 2x8. It was never light: the app gave it the same weight as the heavy day because both days shared one exercise id, and on 2026-08-27 you did 185x6 twice against a 2x8. It is a DB Romanian Deadlift now, which has its own weight and its own history, the way the front squat does against the back squat. THE CUE STILL DESCRIBES THE BARBELL. Read it and say what it should say.

blocks.why: The second hinge of the week, and a different lift rather than a lighter copy of Thursday. Pelland 2025, 67 studies: at matched volume, frequency raises strength (posterior 100%) while size does not care about the split. Nothing in the evidence file ever said the second exposure should be light, and while both days shared one exercise id the app handed this one Thursday heavy weight. Dumbbells have their own ladder and hold no fixture, so this block also stops occupying a rack.

blocks.label: Single Leg + Anti-Lean

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides. Put the top of your back foot on the bench, laces down. Your front foot should be far enough forward that at the bottom your front shin is straight up and down, not leaning forward over your toes. Lower until your back knee is close to the floor. Drive up through the FRONT heel. The back leg is a kickstand, it does not push.

alts.name: DB Step-Up
alts.cue: Bench at about knee height. Drive up through the heel of the foot ON the bench. The trailing foot must not push off the floor. 8/leg.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Step straight backward, drop the back knee toward the floor, push through the FRONT heel to stand. Easier on the knees than stepping forward.

alts.name: Single-Leg Leg Press
alts.cue: One foot in the middle of the platform. Light enough that the working leg does all of it. 8/leg.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
exercises.cue: One heavy dumbbell in ONE hand, nothing in the other. Walk for the seconds shown, standing as tall as you can. The whole exercise is refusing to lean toward the weight: imagine a broomstick down your spine that must stay vertical. Swap hands each set. This trains your side, which nothing else in the programme does. If you cannot stop leaning, the weight is too heavy. COUNT SECONDS, and type the seconds. This one has a hand free, so start the timer as you pick the dumbbell up. Get to the top of the range on time first, then go heavier.

alts.name: Farmer Carry
alts.cue: A heavy dumbbell in EACH hand, stand tall, walk. Easier to balance, trains grip harder, trains the side less.

alts.name: KB Suitcase Hold
alts.cue: One kettlebell in one hand, stand still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this if the floor is too crowded to walk.

exercises.whyHere: Resisting sideways lean. Both loaded, both at the dumbbells, so these two genuinely alternate.

blocks.why: Single-leg strength, and resisting sideways lean. Both loaded, both at the dumbbells, so these two genuinely alternate.

blocks.label: Sideways, then Calves

exercises.name: DB Lateral Lunge
exercises.cue: This is the sideways movement you asked for, and it is loaded on purpose: unweighted band walks were shown to do little. Hold one dumbbell at your chest. Step wide to the LEFT and sit back into that left hip, keeping the right leg straight with the foot flat. Both feet stay pointing forward the whole time. Push off the left foot to come back. You should feel a stretch on the inside of the straight leg and work in the bent leg's hip. Start with a light dumbbell and a small step, then widen the step before you add weight.

alts.name: Cossack Squat
alts.cue: The deeper version. Same sideways sit, but let the straight leg's toes come up and go as low as you can. Bodyweight first, hold a dumbbell at the chest when it is easy. 3x6/side.

alts.name: Lateral Step-Up
alts.cue: Stand side-on to the box. Step UP sideways onto it with the near foot, drive through that heel, lower slowly. 3x8/leg.

alts.name: Banded Lateral Walk
alts.cue: Fallback only, on a day the dumbbells are all taken. Band above the knees, half squat, step sideways keeping the band tight. 3x10/side.

exercises.name: DB Standing Calf Raise
exercises.cue: Done holding dumbbells on the floor by the bench, NOT on the calf machine, so this pairs with the lunge without occupying two machines. Stand on the edge of a step or a plate if you have one, heels hanging. Let the heels sink until you feel a stretch, pause one second at the bottom, then push all the way up onto your toes and squeeze for one second. Slow both directions. This is ankle insurance for the running.

alts.name: Machine Calf Raise
alts.cue: The standing calf machine, if nothing else in this block is running at the same time. Same full stretch and full squeeze.

alts.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
alts.cue: One leg at a time holding one dumbbell, full range. Harder, and closer to what running actually asks of the ankle. 3x12/leg.

open.q: Moved to a dumbbell calf raise on 2026-08-27 to keep it in the lateral lunge rest, and moved back the same night: you worked 180 to 210 lb on the machine and did not touch the dumbbell version. A walk is cheaper than losing 170 lb of load. Its NAME still says DB, which was wrong before today too. What should it be called?

blocks.why: Frontal-plane hip strength is injury insurance for the running: weak abductors feed pelvic drop, which feeds knee valgus, a documented route into shin and knee trouble in novice runners. The calf raise is not sourced. The calf raise follows rather than alternating: it is a machine across the floor, so sharing one rest window would mean walking between them every set.

tuesday.name: Tuesday
tuesday.title: Upper A: press heavy, pull moderate
tuesday.desc: Press heavy, pull moderate, shoulders looked after

blocks.label: Main Lift: DB Bench Press

exercises.name: DB Bench Press
exercises.cue: Feet flat on the floor. Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench and keep them there, like you are pinching a pencil between them. Breathe in, lower the dumbbells until you feel a good stretch across the chest, PAUSE for one second so there is no bounce, then press up and breathe out. The dumbbells travel slightly toward each other at the top but do not clang. ADDED 2026-08-22, after he reported feeling this mostly in the triceps and the front of the shoulder: that is usually where the dumbbells are travelling, not how hard you are pushing. Two things to try. Before the first rep, pull your shoulder blades DOWN and TOGETHER into the bench and keep them pinned there the whole set, so your chest is the highest point and the shoulders cannot roll forward. Then press over your LOWER chest, not your collarbone: at the bottom the dumbbells should be beside your nipples with your elbows about halfway between tucked-in and straight-out, and at the top they finish above the same spot rather than drifting toward your face. Success looks like: at the bottom you feel a stretch across the chest, not a pinch at the front of the shoulder. This is standard coaching practice, not a trial finding.

alts.name: BB Bench Press
alts.cue: Barbell version. Same shoulder blades, same pause on the chest. Easier to load heavy, harder on the shoulders.

alts.name: Machine Chest Press
alts.cue: Set the seat so the handles sit level with the middle of your chest. Same press, no balancing.

alts.name: DB Incline Press
alts.cue: Bench set one or two notches up from flat. Hits the top of the chest and the front of the shoulder more.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.cue: On the floor beside the bench, between press sets. Your example, and it is the pairing that always worked. On your back, arms straight up at the ceiling, knees bent up over your hips. Press your lower back FLAT into the floor and keep it there: that is the entire exercise. Slowly lower one arm behind your head and the opposite leg toward the floor, breathe out as they go. Stop the moment your lower back lifts off the floor, even if the leg is nowhere near down. Come back and swap sides.

alts.name: Hollow Body Hold
alts.cue: Lower back pressed flat into the floor, arms overhead and legs straight and lifted, so your body makes a shallow banana. Bend the knees or keep arms at your sides if the back lifts. 3x20s.

alts.name: Side Plank
alts.cue: On one forearm, body in a straight line from head to heels, hips lifted and held up. Drop to the knees if the hips sag. 3x30s per side.

exercises.whyHere: The dead bug goes in the rest gaps, and it is here for a reason rather than because core is good

blocks.why: Pressing twice a week, heavy here and moderate Friday. The dead bug goes in the rest gaps, and it is here for a reason rather than because core is good: core work moved knee valgus by d = -1.25 to -1.44, the same running insurance as the sideways work.

blocks.label: Overhead

exercises.name: Standing DB Overhead Press
exercises.cue: STANDING, not seated: that is the difference between this and the seated version in the alternatives, and it is why this needs no bench. Done second in the session from 2026-08-22, and the reason is in "Why this is here". Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing forward. Squeeze your bum and tighten your stomach BEFORE you press, so your ribs do not flare and your lower back does not arch. Press straight up until the arms are locked out with the dumbbells over the middle of your head, not in front of your face. Lower under control to the shoulders. Success looks like: your ribs stay down and you can hold the lockout still for a second. If your back arches to start the rep, go lighter.

alts.name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm DB Overhead Press
alts.cue: One knee down, the other foot forward, one dumbbell in the hand on the SAME side as the down knee. Press it straight overhead without letting your ribs flare or your body lean away. It is two exercises at once: a press, and your trunk refusing to bend sideways under a load held on one side. Lighter than the two-dumbbell version by a lot, and that is the point. From The Motion Blueprint (Jason & Lauren Pak, Theory of Motion, 2025), 4-day Day 2 Upper, "C1. Overhead Pressing Variations".

alts.name: BB Overhead Press
alts.cue: Barbell from the rack at collarbone height. Push your head slightly back so the bar clears your face, then forward under it at the top.

alts.name: Machine Shoulder Press
alts.cue: Seat height so the handles start level with your shoulders. Same lockout, no balancing.

alts.name: Seated DB Overhead Press
alts.cue: Bench upright, back supported. Takes the lower back out of it entirely.

blocks.why: The second overhead exposure of the week after Friday machine press, and it is the only main lift that did not move all year: 60x10 in May, 65x8 in June, back to 60x8 in August. Two things were wrong and both are fixed. Its rep range could not reach the next dumbbell (see scripts/check-ladder.mjs), and it sat fourth in the session. Nunes 2021, 11 studies: strength gains are largest in the exercises performed at the beginning of a session. It is second now, which is also the last block whose LEAD is at the dumbbells.

blocks.label: Second Pattern: Vertical Pull

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Sit tall with your thighs locked under the pad. Start with your arms fully straight so you feel the stretch down your sides. Pull your ELBOWS down toward your ribs rather than thinking about your hands, and bring the bar to your upper chest. Let it back up slowly and all the way straight. Building toward real pull-ups.

alts.name: Assisted Pull-up
alts.cue: Set enough counterweight that you get 8 clean reps with a full hang at the bottom and chin over the bar at the top. Reduce the assistance as it gets easy.

alts.name: Pull-up
alts.cue: The bar over the rack. Dead hang, chin over the bar, lower under control. As many clean reps as you have.

alts.name: TRX Row
alts.cue: Straps at the pull-up bar. Lean back with straight arms and a straight body, pull your chest to your hands. Walk your feet forward to make it harder, back to make it easier. 3x10.

exercises.name: Cable Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. ONE dumbbell held in both hands, cupping the top end like a mug. Press it straight overhead, then bend only your elbows to lower it behind your head until you feel a stretch down the back of your arms, about level with the base of your skull. Your upper arms stay pointing at the ceiling and DO NOT drift forward: that is the whole exercise. Straighten the arms to come back up. Success looks like: your elbows stay the same distance apart the whole time and your ribs do not flare forward. If your back arches, go lighter. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: DB Skullcrusher
alts.cue: Lying on a bench, a dumbbell in each hand, bend at the elbow to lower them beside your ears and press back up. Use this if overhead bothers your shoulder.

alts.name: Tricep Pushdown
alts.cue: The cable version, only if the stack you are already standing at is free between sets.

open.q: This slot moved from db-overhead-tricep-extension to cable-overhead-tricep-extension on 2026-08-27 so the partner sits at the lead lift's own station. THE CUE BELOW STILL DESCRIBES THE OLD IMPLEMENT. Read it on the machine and say what it should say.

blocks.why: The week's first vertical pull; the assisted pull-up on Friday is the second. The triceps do nothing during a pulldown, so they are what goes in its rest. A dumbbell comes to the cable stack with you; nothing that needs the floor can, which is why this is not a plank.

blocks.label: Second Horizontal Pull
blocks.why: The second horizontal pull of the week; before 2026-08-22 BB Row on Friday was the only row in seven days, against the rule that every main pattern happens twice (Pelland 2025). The side delt goes in its rest because a row does not use it, and because nothing else in the week does: every press works the front of the shoulder and every row works the back. It replaced a lower-body exercise that was here on 2026-08-22 for no reason anybody could defend, which he spotted from the gym floor.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.cue: Sit tall, knees soft, chest up. Start with your arms straight and let the weight pull your shoulder blades forward, then pull your ELBOWS back past your ribs and squeeze the shoulder blades together at the end. Do not lean back to move it: your torso stays where it started. Let it back out slowly until the arms are straight again.

alts.name: Chest-Supported DB Row
alts.cue: Chest on an incline bench so your torso cannot swing. Row both dumbbells to your ribs, elbows close, squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides, palms facing your thighs, a small bend kept in the elbows. Lift both arms out SIDEWAYS, not forward, until your hands are level with your shoulders and no higher. Lead with the elbows, as if you were pouring from two jugs. Lower slowly, about twice as long coming down as going up. Success looks like: your shoulders do not rise toward your ears, and you can stop the weight dead at the top instead of it swinging. If either fails, go lighter. This is the SIDE of the shoulder, and it is the one thing nothing else in the week trains: every press works the front, every row works the back. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: Seated DB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same raise, sitting on the end of a bench. Sitting stops you swinging, so use it if the standing version keeps turning into a heave.

alts.name: Kettlebell Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same movement with the lightest kettlebells, held by the handle. Use them if the light dumbbells are gone.

open.q: This slot moved from db-lateral-raise to cable-lateral-raise on 2026-08-27 so the partner sits at the lead lift's own station. THE CUE BELOW STILL DESCRIBES THE OLD IMPLEMENT. Read it on the machine and say what it should say.

Moved to the cable on 2026-08-27 and moved back the same hour: the seated row holds the low pulley and a cable lateral raise needs the adjustable column, so the two cannot share one rest window. A dumbbell holds nothing and travels, which is why the partner is a dumbbell.

Five lifts cannot reach their own next weight, this one twice over: at 20 lb, the top of 12 to 14 reps banks an estimated 29.3 and the next dumbbell up demands 35.0, so maxing out the range earns a jump you will fail. The others are the DB lateral lunge, the assisted pull-up and the DB reverse fly. Two ways out and they apply to all five. Widen the rep range so the top of it actually earns the jump, which here means 12 to 23 reps and a long set. Or accept that these four stall at their current weight and progress only on reps. Which one, and is a 23-rep set of lateral raises something you would actually do?

blocks.label: Triceps + Biceps

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown
exercises.cue: Cable high, rope or straight bar. Pin your elbows to your sides and keep them there: only the forearms move. Push down until the arms are completely straight, hold half a second, then let it come up slowly until you feel the stretch. If your elbows drift forward or you lean over the bar, drop the weight.

alts.name: EZ Bar Skullcrusher
alts.cue: Lying on a bench with the EZ bar. Keep the upper arms still and pointing at the ceiling, bend only at the elbow to lower the bar toward your forehead, then straighten. Light.

alts.name: Assisted Dip
alts.cue: Enough counterweight for 8 to 10 clean reps. Stay fairly upright to bias the triceps, lean forward to bias the chest.

exercises.name: DB Hammer Curl
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand hanging by your sides, palms facing IN toward your thighs and STAYING that way the whole rep: that is what makes it a hammer curl instead of a normal curl. Pin your elbows against your ribs. Bend the elbow and bring the dumbbell up toward your shoulder, then lower it all the way until the arm is straight. Success looks like: your elbows have not travelled forward and your body has not swung to start the rep. If it swings, go lighter. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: DB Biceps Curl
alts.cue: Same movement with the palms turned UP the whole way instead of facing in. Same muscle, slightly different angle.

alts.name: Kettlebell Curl
alts.cue: A kettlebell in each hand by the handle, same elbow-pinned curl. The weight hangs behind your hand, which makes the top half harder.

open.q: This slot moved from db-hammer-curl to cable-curl on 2026-08-27 so the partner sits at the lead lift's own station. THE CUE BELOW STILL DESCRIBES THE OLD IMPLEMENT. Read it on the machine and say what it should say.
Same reason: the pushdown holds the high pulley and a cable curl needs the low one. Two cable exercises are only one station when they are the same column.

blocks.why: Arms do not earn twice a week on the frequency evidence, so this block is first to go when time is short. It does not follow that arms get one exposure: counted across the week they get three each, because every partner slot that needed filling got filled with an arm or a delt. That is a live problem with the file and not a justification. Pushdown and curl are direct opposites, which is the pairing the review actually studied: antagonist preloading facilitates the second lift rather than blunting it.

blocks.label: Anti-Rotation + Rear Delts

exercises.name: Cable Pallof Press
exercises.cue: Set the cable at chest height. Stand SIDEWAYS to the machine, feet shoulder width, and hold the handle at your breastbone with both hands. The cable is now trying to twist you toward it. Press your hands straight out in front of your chest until the arms are locked, hold for two seconds, and come back to your chest. The whole exercise is refusing to rotate: your shoulders and hips stay square to the wall in front of you. Success looks like: someone standing behind you could not tell which side the cable is on from the way your body is facing. If your ribs twist toward the machine, stand closer or go lighter. Do all reps one side, then turn around. Added 2026-08-22 from The Motion Blueprint (Jason & Lauren Pak, Theory of Motion, 2025), 3-day Day 3, "C2. Multi-Planar / Anti-Rotation".

alts.name: Band Pallof Press
alts.cue: Band anchored at chest height on a rack post, stand sideways, both hands on the band at your chest. Press straight out and resist the twist, hold 2 seconds. Only if every cable column is taken: there is no way to record which band you used, so the number cannot move.

alts.name: Half-Kneeling Cable Pallof Press
alts.cue: Same press, kneeling on the knee CLOSEST to the machine with the other foot forward. Kneeling takes the legs out of it, so the only thing that can stop the twist is your trunk. Harder at the same weight.

exercises.name: Cable Reverse Fly
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand. Push your hips back and lean your chest forward to about 45 degrees, roughly halfway to parallel with the floor, back flat, eyes down. Let the dumbbells hang straight below your chest with a small bend in the elbows. Now open your arms out to the SIDES like opening a pair of curtains, until your hands are level with your shoulders. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly. Success looks like: your torso does not rise as you lift, and you feel it between the shoulder blades rather than in your lower back. Go light, this is a small muscle. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: Chest-Supported Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Same movement lying face down on an incline bench, which removes the lower back entirely. Use this if the standing version makes your back ache.

alts.name: Rear Delt Machine
alts.cue: The fly machine turned around. Arms out and back, squeeze the shoulder blades, no jerking.

open.q: Why does the reverse fly sit in the Cable Pallof rest? This block's why is entirely about anti-rotation and never mentions the fly, so there is no clause to show on the card.

This slot moved from db-reverse-fly to cable-reverse-fly on 2026-08-27 so the partner sits at the lead lift's own station. THE CUE BELOW STILL DESCRIBES THE OLD IMPLEMENT. Read it on the machine and say what it should say.

blocks.why: The week trained the trunk to resist bending forward and never once to resist TWISTING. The Motion Blueprint (Jason & Lauren Pak, Theory of Motion, 2025) trains the core in eight patterns and this was the missing one. It was cut on 2026-08-15 because equipment.json marked the adjustable cable column "unknown", and on 2026-08-22 he said every column in the building adjusts, which is the only reason this is back. Core work earns its place on the evidence already in the file: Comert & Gruber 2025, core strengthening d = -1.25 to -1.44 for knee valgus, which is the thing that matters once you start running.

thursday.name: Thursday
thursday.title: Lower B: hinge heavy, second squat
thursday.desc: Hinge heavy, squat light, sideways explosive

blocks.label: Power Primer

exercises.name: Lateral Bound
exercises.cue: Replaces the broad jump, which you swapped out every single time. This is the sideways explosive work you asked for. Stand on your LEFT leg. Push off it sideways and land on your RIGHT leg only, then FREEZE completely still for two seconds before going back. Land with the knee bent and pointing over your toes, never caving inward. Only jump as far as you can land and freeze. Success looks like: silent landing, no wobble, no second little hop to catch yourself. If you cannot freeze it, go shorter.

alts.name: Box Jump
alts.cue: Straight ahead instead of sideways. Jump onto the box, land soft and quiet with bent knees, STEP down. 3x3.

alts.name: Lateral Line Hop
alts.cue: The easier version. Both feet together, hop side to side over a line on the floor, small and fast, staying on the balls of your feet. 3x15.

alts.name: Pogo Hops
alts.cue: Small fast bounces on the balls of your feet, stiff ankles. 3x15.

open.q: The card says 3 sets of 3 and on 2026-08-27 you logged 10 reps a set. One of the two is wrong and nobody has established which. Note #20 asks how to progress these: a taller box is not the answer (stepping down removes the landing, so height mostly buys a deeper tuck, not more force) and neither is more reps. What is left is intent and ground contact time, and NO trial was found for that ladder, so it is not going on a card until it is sourced. How many did you mean to do?

exercises.name: DB Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides, palms facing your thighs, a small bend kept in the elbows. Lift both arms out SIDEWAYS, not forward, until your hands are level with your shoulders and no higher. Lead with the elbows, as if you were pouring from two jugs. Lower slowly, about twice as long coming down as going up. Success looks like: your shoulders do not rise toward your ears, and you can stop the weight dead at the top instead of it swinging. If either fails, go lighter. This is the SIDE of the shoulder, and it is the one thing nothing else in the week trains: every press works the front, every row works the back. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: Seated DB Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same raise, sitting on the end of a bench. Sitting stops you swinging, so use it if the standing version keeps turning into a heave.

alts.name: Kettlebell Lateral Raise
alts.cue: Same movement with the lightest kettlebells, held by the handle. Use them if the light dumbbells are gone.

exercises.whyHere: The lateral raise rides in the rest for the same reason as Monday: it is upper body, so the bound stays fresh.

blocks.why: Same reasoning and dose as Monday jumps, done sideways. First and fresh, progressed by quality and contact count rather than distance. The lateral raise rides in the rest for the same reason as Monday: it is upper body, so the bound stays fresh.

blocks.label: Main Lift: Romanian Deadlift

exercises.name: BB Romanian Deadlift
exercises.cue: The heavy hinge, the one we progress. Breathe IN and tighten your stomach. Bar stays touching your legs the whole way, shins vertical. Bend the knees slightly and then FREEZE them, then push your hips backward toward the wall behind you. Go down until you feel a strong stretch down the back of your thighs, usually around knee height, and no further. Squeeze your bum and snap the hips forward to stand up, breathing out at the top. If your lower back rounds you have gone too far down. STRAPS, because you asked on 18 August: yes, use them, and they will not cost you anything here. Do the first warm-up set with bare hands so you keep noticing what your grip is doing, then strap up for all four working sets. The hamstrings are what this lift is for, and stopping a set because the bar is slipping out of your fingers trains neither. Your grip is not being neglected either: the Farmer Carry on Friday and the Suitcase Carry on Monday are both held bare-handed and that is where grip is meant to be worked. This is standard coaching practice rather than something a trial has tested, so it is a convention, not evidence.

alts.name: DB Romanian Deadlift
alts.cue: Two heavy dumbbells in front of your thighs. Same hip push backward, same freeze in the knees.

alts.name: Smith RDL
alts.cue: Bar on rails so it cannot drift away from your legs. Useful for grooving the hinge when you are tired.

alts.name: Leg Curl
alts.cue: Direct hamstring work with no load on the lower back. Use it on a day your back is cooked. Squeeze at the top, lower slowly. 4x10.

open.q: You asked for hanging knee raises in this lift's rest, holding the top of the rack you are already standing at. The data will not allow it yet: the rack and the pull-up bar on top of it are two separate stations in equipment.json, and a paired block may hold only one fixture. So, standing there: while you are in the rack with a loaded bar, could another member use that pull-up bar? If no, the bar is part of the rack and the file should say so, and this pairing ships. If yes, they are genuinely two fixtures and the knee raise cannot ride in this rest.

And how much trunk work do you actually want. Abdominals are already at 16 fractional sets a week, past the top of the efficient zone at 10, which you can now see on /health under Volume. Three sets of knee raises here takes them to 19. Option 1, add them anyway: past the efficient zone means each extra set buys less, not that it hurts. Option 2, add nothing and move work that is already in the week into these rest gaps instead, for example the single-leg RDL from the front squat day, which costs zero new sets. Option 1 or option 2.

blocks.why: The heavy hinge, the one that gets progressed. Squat went 135x10 to 185x6 since May while this pattern ran twice a week.

blocks.label: Second Pattern: Squat

exercises.name: Front Squat
exercises.cue: Your second squat of the week, deliberately light. This is the technique fix: because the bar sits on the FRONT of your shoulders, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier, which is exactly what a back squat struggles with. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Let your fingertips just hook under the bar, the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. If the elbows drop, the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
alts.cue: Same upright effect with a dumbbell held at the chest, and no wrist or elbow demand at all. The easiest way to feel a deep upright squat.

alts.name: BB Back Squat
alts.cue: Light back squat instead, about 60% of Monday's weight. Use this if the front rack position hurts your wrists.

alts.name: Smith Squat
alts.cue: On rails. Feet slightly forward of the bar. Same depth, no balance demand.

blocks.why: The week second squat, and a different lift rather than a lighter copy of Monday: the front squat carries its own weight and its own history. Same frequency argument as the second hinge on Lower A. The reverse fly rides in the rest because a front squat uses nothing in the upper back except to hold position, and the rest was being spent either way.

blocks.label: Lunge

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up. Stepping backward rather than forward keeps the load off the front knee.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

alts.name: DB Step-Up
alts.cue: Bench at knee height, drive through the heel of the top foot. 8/leg.

blocks.why: Single-leg work, dead bugs in the rest gaps for the same knee-valgus reason as Tuesday.

blocks.label: Single-Leg Hinge + Groin

exercises.name: Single-Leg RDL
exercises.cue: Has sat at 40 lb since May, so this time the weight moves, not just the reps. One dumbbell in the hand OPPOSITE the standing leg. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent and frozen. Push the hip backward and let the free leg extend straight behind you like a see-saw, keeping your hips square to the floor: the back hip must not open toward the ceiling. Go until you feel the hamstring stretch, then stand and squeeze. Slow. Touch the bench with your free toe if you lose balance.

alts.name: B-Stance RDL
alts.cue: Back toe lightly touching the floor for balance, but almost all the weight on the front leg. Much easier to balance, so you can load it heavier.

alts.name: KB Single-Leg RDL
alts.cue: Same movement holding a kettlebell. The handle sits closer to your leg, which some people find easier to control. 8/leg.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank (short lever)
exercises.cue: The groin and inner-thigh half of the sideways work, and the piece nothing in the old programme trained at all. START WITH THE EASY VERSION: lie on your side with your bottom forearm on the floor, and put your TOP KNEE (not the foot) on the bench. Lift your hips off the floor so your body is a straight line, squeezing the bench with the top leg. Hold for the seconds shown. Your bottom leg hangs free. When 3 sets of 20 seconds feels controlled, move the top FOOT to the bench instead of the knee, which is much harder. Expect this to be humbling. Stop if you feel a sharp pull in the groin. Count the seconds in your head, one thousand one, one thousand two: you are on one forearm and cannot reach the phone. The count is the number you type.

alts.name: Adductor Ball Squeeze
alts.cue: The gentlest version. On your back, knees bent, a ball or rolled towel between the knees. Squeeze it hard for the seconds shown and breathe. 3x20s.

alts.name: Side Plank w/ Leg Lift
alts.cue: Side plank on the forearm, then lift the TOP leg toward the ceiling and hold. Trains the outside of the hip instead of the inside. 3x20s per side.

exercises.whyHere: The Copenhagen appears nowhere in the evidence file: common practice, not a trial.

blocks.why: Single-leg hinge, and the Copenhagen for the groin. The Copenhagen appears nowhere in the evidence file: common practice, not a trial.

blocks.label: Hamstrings + Calves

exercises.name: Leg Curl Machine
exercises.cue: Lying or seated depending on which machine is free. Set the pad so it sits just ABOVE your heels, on the Achilles, not on your calf. Lie or sit with your knees lined up with the machine pivot, the bolt the arm turns on. Curl your heels toward your bum as far as the machine allows, pause for one second at the tightest point, then lower slowly, taking about twice as long down as up. Success looks like: your hips stay flat on the pad and do not lift as you curl. If they lift, go lighter. This is the only exercise in the week that bends the knee against resistance: every other hamstring movement here is a hinge, where the hamstring works at the hip instead. Added 2026-08-22 from The Motion Blueprint (Jason & Lauren Pak, Theory of Motion, 2025), 4-day Day 1 Lower, "D1. Isolation Hamstrings".

alts.name: Stability Ball Hamstring Curl
alts.cue: The version their programme actually names, if the machine is taken and a ball is free. On your back, heels on the ball, hips lifted, roll the ball in toward you by bending the knees, then roll it back out slowly without letting the hips drop.

alts.name: Back Extension
alts.cue: On the 45 degree pad, hugging a plate. Not the same movement, it works the hamstring at the hip like everything else here, but it is the closest thing if the leg curl is taken.

exercises.name: DB Standing Calf Raise
exercises.cue: Done holding dumbbells at the machine bank, standing, so it needs no fixture of its own. Stand on the edge of a step or a plate if you have one, heels hanging. Let the heels sink until you feel a stretch, pause one second at the bottom, then push all the way up onto your toes and squeeze for one second. Slow both directions. This is ankle insurance for the running.

alts.name: Machine Calf Raise
alts.cue: The standing calf machine, if nothing else in this block is running at the same time. Same full stretch and full squeeze.

alts.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
alts.cue: One leg at a time holding one dumbbell, full range. Harder, and closer to what running actually asks of the ankle. 3x12/leg.

exercises.whyHere: Calves are twice a week here and the evidence file does not ask for that

blocks.why: Two holes in the week, both filled on the day they belong to. The hamstring only ever worked at the HIP here, in the RDLs; nothing bent the knee against resistance, and the leg curl is the only machine in the building that does. Calves are twice a week here and the evidence file does not ask for that: it says squat, hinge, press and pull go twice, and that arms, calves and delts do not need to. This is also where a calf raise actually belongs: it was briefly on Tuesday paired with a cable row, he asked why, and he was right. The Motion Blueprint (Jason & Lauren Pak, Theory of Motion, 2025) pairs calves with the hinge on a lower day, which is the same reasoning.

friday.name: Friday
friday.title: Upper B: pull heavy, press moderate
friday.desc: Pull heavy, press moderate, swim catch

blocks.label: Main Lift: BB Row

exercises.name: BB Row
exercises.cue: This has been stuck at 165 lb since May because it always came fifth, when you were already cooked. It now leads the day, so it should move. Hinge forward until your chest is roughly parallel to the floor, knees slightly bent, back flat. Breathe in and brace. Pull the bar to your belly button by driving your ELBOWS backward past your ribs, then lower it all the way under control. Your torso does not move: if you are standing up a little to help the bar, it is too heavy.

alts.name: Chest-Supported Row
alts.cue: Chest on an incline bench, dumbbells hanging. The bench removes the lower back entirely, so nothing can cheat. Good on a day the RDLs left your back tired.

alts.name: Seated Cable Row
alts.cue: Tall chest, pull the handle to your stomach, squeeze the shoulder blades, let it stretch all the way forward.

alts.name: TRX Row
alts.cue: Straps at the pull-up bar. Body straight, pull your chest to your hands. Walk the feet forward to make it harder. 4x10.

blocks.why: Pulling twice a week, heavy here and moderate Tuesday. Six loaded pulling sets in a week is the thinnest part of the programme, which is why this is the spine of the day and leads it.

blocks.label: Second Pattern: Horizontal Press

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
exercises.cue: Your second press of the week, moderate rather than heavy: Tuesday is the day the bench gets pushed. Machine on purpose, so a tired chest does not have to balance dumbbells. Set the seat so the handles line up with the MIDDLE of your chest. Press out until the arms are straight without locking hard, then come back slowly until you feel the stretch. Shoulder blades stay pinned back against the pad.

alts.name: DB Incline Press
alts.cue: Bench one or two notches up from flat, dumbbells. More work for the top of the chest and the shoulders.

alts.name: Chest Fly Machine
alts.cue: Elbows slightly bent and fixed, bring the arms together in front of you and squeeze for one second. Stretch, not a press.

alts.name: Assisted Dip
alts.cue: Lean your chest forward to bias the chest. Enough counterweight for 8 clean reps. You had 5 strict dips in May, so this is trackable.

blocks.why: The second press of the week, moderate. It CANNOT share a window with the row: the row holds a rack and this holds a machine, and the validator refuses that pairing. What it CAN share it with is a pair of dumbbells, which you carry in. Biceps do nothing during a chest press, so that is what goes there. He asked on 2026-08-25 whether more of this day could have happened at the barbell station he started at (note #14), and ruled on 2026-08-27 to keep the machines. The barbell versions do exist: he has logged BB bench to 185 and BB OHP to 115 in that rack. What a machine buys is the cheap half of a twice-a-week pattern, which is the entire reason a second exposure is not a second heavy one. The walking is already bounded by a gate rather than by good intentions: validate.mjs refuses a day whose route doubles back, so Friday visits the rack, the machines, the cable stack and the preacher seat once each and finishes with each before leaving it.

blocks.label: Second Vertical Pull
blocks.why: The second vertical pull. Lat Pulldown on Tuesday was the only one in the week, against the same twice-a-week rule the rest of the programme follows. The counterweight is the load and it goes DOWN as you get stronger, which is a progression with a finish line: an unassisted pull-up. Side delts go in the rest because a pull-up does not use them.

exercises.name: Assisted Pull-Up
exercises.cue: Set the counterweight so you get 6 clean reps: full hang with straight arms at the bottom, chin over the bar at the top. Log the COUNTERWEIGHT, and remember it is the one number here that should go DOWN over time. When 6 feels easy, take 10 lb of assistance off.

alts.name: Lat Pulldown
alts.cue: If the assisted machine is taken. Same job, elbows down to the ribs, all the way straight at the top.

blocks.label: Second Overhead Press
blocks.why: The second shoulder press. DB Overhead Press on Tuesday was the only one, and it is the pattern with the least to show for the year: 65x8 in July, back to 60x8 now. A machine on the second exposure keeps it cheap. The reverse fly is the antagonist of a press, so it rides in the rest and may even help the next set.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.cue: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height, not above your ears. Press up until your arms are straight without shrugging, and come back down slowly until the handles are level with your shoulders again. Stop the set when your lower back starts arching off the pad.

alts.name: Seated DB Overhead Press
alts.cue: Bench upright, dumbbells at shoulder height, press up and slightly together. Ribs down, no arch.

exercises.name: DB Reverse Fly
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. A dumbbell in each hand. Push your hips back and lean your chest forward to about 45 degrees, roughly halfway to parallel with the floor, back flat, eyes down. Let the dumbbells hang straight below your chest with a small bend in the elbows. Now open your arms out to the SIDES like opening a pair of curtains, until your hands are level with your shoulders. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly. Success looks like: your torso does not rise as you lift, and you feel it between the shoulder blades rather than in your lower back. Go light, this is a small muscle. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: Chest-Supported Reverse Fly
alts.cue: Same movement lying face down on an incline bench, which removes the lower back entirely. Use this if the standing version makes your back ache.

alts.name: Rear Delt Machine
alts.cue: The fly machine turned around. Arms out and back, squeeze the shoulder blades, no jerking.

open.q: This slot moved from db-reverse-fly to pec-deck-reverse on 2026-08-27 so the partner sits at the lead lift's own station. THE CUE BELOW STILL DESCRIBES THE OLD IMPLEMENT. Read it on the machine and say what it should say.
Same reason: the shoulder press machine and the pec deck are two separate fixtures.

blocks.label: Swim Catch + Triceps

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.cue: This is your freestyle catch trained directly, which is why it stays even though the rest of the day changed. Cable set high, rope or straight bar, stand back a step and hinge slightly forward. Arms stay STRAIGHT the whole time, elbows barely bent and locked there. Sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs and squeeze the muscles down the sides of your back, then let it float back up. Much lighter than a lat pulldown, because straight arms are a long lever.

alts.name: Band Straight-Arm Pulldown
alts.cue: Band anchored high on a rack post. Identical arc with straight arms. Use it when the cables are all busy.

alts.name: DB Pullover
alts.cue: Lying across or along a bench, one dumbbell held over the chest with near-straight arms. Lower it behind your head until you feel the stretch under the armpits, then pull it back over. 3x12.

exercises.name: Cable Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.cue: Standing, in the rest between sets of the lift above. ONE dumbbell held in both hands, cupping the top end like a mug. Press it straight overhead, then bend only your elbows to lower it behind your head until you feel a stretch down the back of your arms, about level with the base of your skull. Your upper arms stay pointing at the ceiling and DO NOT drift forward: that is the whole exercise. Straighten the arms to come back up. Success looks like: your elbows stay the same distance apart the whole time and your ribs do not flare forward. If your back arches, go lighter. First time out, pick a weight you are sure you could lift 15 times and stop at 12.

alts.name: DB Skullcrusher
alts.cue: Lying on a bench, a dumbbell in each hand, bend at the elbow to lower them beside your ears and press back up. Use this if overhead bothers your shoulder.

alts.name: Tricep Pushdown
alts.cue: The cable version, only if the stack you are already standing at is free between sets.

open.q: This slot moved from db-overhead-tricep-extension to cable-overhead-tricep-extension on 2026-08-27 so the partner sits at the lead lift's own station. THE CUE BELOW STILL DESCRIBES THE OLD IMPLEMENT. Read it on the machine and say what it should say.

blocks.why: Straight-arm pulldown for the catch position in the water. Not sourced in the evidence file, and it stays because it is loadable and it is the one lift here aimed at the swim. Triceps go in its rest: a straight-arm pull is all lat and no elbow, so they are idle.

blocks.label: Biceps, then Carry

exercises.name: Incline DB Curl
exercises.cue: The zed bar with the seat, which you have had all along and which was never written down anywhere. Sit with the backs of your upper arms flat on the slanted pad and keep them there. Grip the angled part of the bar so your wrists sit comfortably. Curl up until your forearms are vertical, squeeze, then lower ALL THE WAY until the arms are straight. The pad is the point: it makes swinging impossible, so the weight will feel heavier than a standing curl. Start lighter than you think.

alts.name: DB Bicep Curl
alts.cue: Standing, dumbbells, elbows still at your sides, no swinging. Squeeze at the top, lower slowly.

alts.name: Cable Curl
alts.cue: Low cable with a straight or EZ attachment. The cable keeps tension on the muscle at every point, including the top where dumbbells go light. 3x12.

alts.name: Hammer Curl
alts.cue: Thumbs up the whole way, like holding two hammers. Hits the forearm and the outside of the arm too.

open.q: This slot moved from ez-preacher-curl to incline-db-curl on 2026-08-27 so the partner sits at the lead lift's own station. THE CUE BELOW STILL DESCRIBES THE OLD IMPLEMENT. Read it on the machine and say what it should say.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.cue: Done after the curls rather than alternating with them, because it needs room to walk and the preacher seat does not travel. A heavy dumbbell in each hand, stand as tall as you can, shoulders back, stomach tight, and walk for the seconds shown. Grip, posture and everything down your sides at once. Put them down before your form falls apart, not after. COUNT SECONDS, and type the seconds. Start the watch before you pick the dumbbells up, because you cannot press anything with both hands full. Get to the top of the range on time first, then go heavier.

alts.name: Suitcase Carry
alts.cue: One dumbbell only. Much harder on the side you are NOT carrying, because it has to stop you leaning. Swap hands each set.

alts.name: KB Farmer Carry
alts.cue: Kettlebells instead, and THE RACK STOPS AT 50 LB EACH: that is the whole set, 20 up to 50, two of each. His note #18, 2026-08-25: 'Therea no kettlebell after 50 for farmers'. He is right, and it is why the prescribed version is dumbbells, which go to 90 and which he has already carried at 75 per hand. Use this one when the dumbbells are taken, not when you want it heavier. They hang differently and swing a little, so the grip works harder at the same weight.

alts.name: DB Static Hold
alts.cue: Heavy dumbbells held at your sides, standing still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this when the floor is too crowded to walk.

exercises.whyHere: The carry follows rather than alternating: it needs room to walk, so alternating means giving up the bench

blocks.why: This is the third biceps exposure of the week, not the first: DB Hammer Curl runs on Tuesday and again on Friday. An earlier version of this line said biceps get one a week, which the same file falsifies. Kassiano 2022 is the reason this one is an incline curl: the shoulder sits BEHIND the torso so the biceps work lengthened, which is a different stimulus from Tuesday rather than the same curl with a different handle. The carry follows rather than alternating: it needs room to walk, so alternating means giving up the bench. That was true before 2026-08-22, I overrode it that afternoon to make every block a superset, and it was wrong. The Motion Blueprint makes the same caveat: supersets are "logistically challenging in a busy gym setting".
